atlas.statement: The regime is stagflation-lite under a hiking Fed, which permits owning cash flow and pricing power but not duration or crowded AI beta. Because CPI is 3.7%, the 10-year sits at 4.9% with a real yield of 2.6%, and a hike near 77% priced for December (unconfirmed), rates are the binding constraint on valuation. The election relief rally is real but breadth, not the Nasdaq, is carrying it. I hold substantial cash and short-dated Treasuries, plus low-beta health care and staples, banks, and a modest energy hedge against an Iran deal failing. My bias is seeing the cycle early; a CPI print on Nov 10 at or below 0.2% month on month, with yields falling, would make me add risk. A hot print or a 10-year above 5.2% would cut it.

MSFT, NVDA, MU, AVGO, GOOG and APH are all one factor, about 20% of the book at my sizing. The index holds up because equal-weight, health care and staples carry it. I own the great product, not the great price. So I shrink the one-factor sleeve and add breadth outside AI.

Treasury yield and inflation prints (CPI in mid-November)

QQQ.summary: Invesco QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, heavily weighted toward mega-cap technology and AI names. It is down 9% over a month and 4% last week after Texas data-center and midterm news, and is below its 50-day average.

QQQ.bear: Highest beta among the broad funds (1.45) in a risk-off tape; data-center moratorium fears and AI capex debate; technology sector down 7% over 1 month.

Data-center and AI regulation headlines from states

Down 9% over one month, below 50-day average

VTI.summary: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF tracks the entire US equity market, including large, mid and small caps. It is roughly flat over three months and sits 2% off highs, with the same market risks as the S&P 500.

scout:
**WISE COUNCIL: SCOUT DISPATCH, Wed 4 Nov 2026, about 17:20 GMT**

**LEAD: A blue wave removes election risk, but AI is the weak spot**

Stocks jumped Wednesday after Democrats won decisively in the midterms and Trump accepted the result. 
The S&P 500 gained 1.7% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.9%.
 
Intraday quotes put the S&P at 7,699.82 and the Dow at 53,282.50, up about 2.9%.
 The overnight swing was large. 
Nasdaq 100 futures were down as much as 2.5% as the first results came in Tuesday night.


The rally is not uniform, and the split matters for the council.
- **AI and data-center names lagged.** 
Nvidia fell 1.5% in early trade and was the heaviest weight on the S&P.
 
CoreWeave dropped about 10% as the Democratic wins hit data-center sentiment.
 The stated risk is that 
any broad slowing of data-center construction could endanger the investments many top companies have made.

- **Other losers:** 
Trump Media fell 12%
 and 
Tesla fell about 3%.

- **Winners:** 
Renewables and health stocks rallied.

- **Volatility and gold:** 
The VIX fell to about 17, and gold rose to about $4,073.

- **Seasonality:** 
Stocks historically do well in the six months after a midterm.
 Yahoo's warning is that the hard part comes next. I could not confirm sector rotation beyond the first hours.

**SENTIMENT: Tech was in a rout before the vote**


At Tuesday's open, 51% of Nasdaq-100 stocks were in a bear market, down 20% or more from highs.
 
Friday's equity sell-off, led by tech, sent investors into Treasurys.
 Chips bounced Tuesday. 
Sandisk, Micron, Intel, Applied Materials, AMD and Arm each rose 3% or more.
 The tape is fragile and two-way.

**THE AI CAPEX VERDICT (last week's prints)**
- **Alphabet:** One outlet reports 
shares sank 11% as capex of $51B pushed free cash flow to negative $9B for a second straight quarter.
 Treat the size of the drop as single-sourced. Another source says Alphabet held its capex guide at 
$195–205B.

- **Microsoft:** 
It trimmed its capex forecast to $170B from $175B.
 
It beat on earnings and revenue, with Azure up 48%.
 
Its CFO said third-party AI chip delays push some capacity into the first half of 2027.
 
Free cash flow was +$19B.

- **Meta:** 
Full-year capex guidance is $135–145B, with the bottom of the range raised.

- **Amazon:** 
It slipped on its report.
 
The concerns are slowing high-margin ad growth and AI agents disintermediating e-commerce.

- **Market read:** 
Investors now focus on cash-flow returns, not on rewarding spend.
 Microsoft is seen as the cleanest funder. Alphabet and Meta are the cash-burn worries.
- **Apple:** It dropped on Election Day. 
It reported on an unusual Monday schedule.
 I could not confirm the cause of the drop.

**MACRO: The Fed is hiking, and that is the key regime fact**
- **The Fed:** 
It held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28, with a 10–2 vote.
 
The two dissenters wanted a quarter-point hike.
 
Chair Kevin Warsh led a unanimous September hike, the first since 2023.

- **December odds (unconfirmed):** One aggregator shows 
a 77.4% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting as of Nov 4.
 I could not cross-check this against CME directly. Another piece cites under 10% for the October meeting, which is a different meeting.
- **Inflation:** 
CPI ran 3.7% year on year in September, up from 3.4%.

- **Yields:** 
The 10-year is about 4.90%, the 2-year 4.57% and the 30-year 5.29%.
 
Last month the 30-year hit 5.47% and the 10-year 5.18%, the highest in decades.
 Treasury sets its auction sizes today.
- **Oil and Iran:** 
The conflict is eight months old, and reports say Washington and Tehran are seeking a diplomatic exit.
 
Brent fell 7.6% Monday to $104.77.
 
Crude fell more than 8% Wednesday after Vance blamed the war for the election losses.
 Brent was at $117 only days ago. A real deal would cut inflation pressure and hurt XOM, CVX, COP and CNQ.
- **Bitcoin:** 
It is about $80,000.


**CALENDAR: Next two weeks, with the confirmed and unconfirmed items**
- **Today, Nov 4:** ISM services (expected 54.8). Earnings: ARM and QCOM after the close, plus CVS, MCD, NVO, UBER, MCK and TM. Treasury auction sizes. Riksbank decision.
- **Thu, Nov 5:** Bank of England and Norges Bank decisions. Earnings: CNQ, COP, PH, SONY.
- **Fri, Nov 6:** Jobs report (consensus 63K). BRK.B earnings. A weak print against a hawkish Fed is the stagflation test.
- **Tue, Nov 10:** 
October CPI at 8:30am New York time.
 
It is the last inflation reading before the Dec 9 meeting.
 This is the decisive macro event of the window.
- **Wed, Nov 11:** CSCO earnings.
- **Thu, Nov 12:** AMAT after the close.
- **Fri, Nov 13:** PPI. MUFG, MFG and SMFG earnings.
- **Tue, Nov 17:** Retail sales. 
NVDA reports after the close, a date marked confirmed by one source.
 
Consensus is EPS $2.47 on revenue of $108.82B.
 
The last quarter was $96.2B, up 106%,
 and 
the stock moved 7% on that print.
 Also HD, DIS, BHP, MDT and PDD.
- **Wed, Nov 18:** 
FOMC minutes at 2:00pm ET.
 LOW, TJX and PANW (after the close).
- **Thu, Nov 19:** WMT.
- **Nov 24–25:** BABA, ADI and DELL on the 24th. GDP, PCE and DE on the 25th.
- **Dec 9:** FOMC, just beyond the window.

**EARNINGS CONTEXT**
- Zacks reports tech Q3 earnings up 
+42.5% on +30.1% revenue, with 84.1% beating EPS estimates.
 
Excluding Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet, S&P growth falls to +26.5% from +43.4%.
 Fundamentals are strong, but the market is punishing the cash burn.
- AMD: 
It reported much stronger profit than expected but rose only modestly.
 
It is paying OpenAI and Meta in stock.

- Super Micro: 
It jumped more than 9% after beating estimates.

- SpaceX (SPCX): 
It signed a deal with Qualcomm and is nearing status as a fourth US carrier. Shares fell about 3%.


**BOLD READ**
The election gave a relief bid, but the real drivers are three things. The first is the CPI print on Nov 10 against a Fed that wants to hike. The second is oil and any Iran deal. The third is whether Nvidia on Nov 17 can restore faith in AI spending. Cheap, battered chips and memory are bouncing, while hyperscaler free cash flow and data-center policy remain open questions. Renewables, health care and rate-sensitive domestic names are the policy-clarity beneficiaries.

**Unconfirmed:**
- The Alphabet drop size.
- The December hike odds.
- Midterm policy details such as data-center rules.
- The specific causes of Apple's and Amazon's moves.

redteam.statement: The portfolio's biggest hole is the 26.9% SHY block. It is called a hedge, but it is a bet on one outcome: a hot CPI on Nov 10 with the Fed hiking. At 4.6% it pays roughly 0.4% over three weeks. A soft CPI plus a strong NVDA guide on Nov 17 leaves 27% of capital idle, while 8 seats own the same 5 names. I also see hidden correlation. VZ, CB, ABBV, V, JPM, PFE and RSP are sold as separate hedges, but they are one crowded defensive trade, and RSI is 70-76 on several of them. MSFT at 7.5% carries 29x earnings and a 1.5% FCF yield, and it is the only AI name still holding trend. Part of this is sound: the AI sleeve is capped near 14%, and UBER and JPM have already reported.

attacks.argument: 26.9% in a 2-year note that is a pure rate bet. It pays about 0.4% in three weeks, and in a soft-CPI relief rally the drag is large. It is also a one-sided macro call dressed as safety.
Defensive crowding: VZ, ABBV, V, CB, PFE, XLV, RSP and PG are all up 10-20% in a month and at highs. A bond rally or rotation hits them together. The 'uncorrelated hedges' share one factor.

7.5% in the largest position at 29x earnings and a 1.5% FCF yield, 27% above its 200d. It is the cleanest AI name, but a hot CPI or weak NVDA guide on Nov 17 hits it first. A $25B debt sale adds leverage.
5.2% on a 20% FCF yield that the market is not paying for. The SpaceX-Qualcomm carrier entry is a structural threat, and TMUS and T fell on it. The yield may be a value-trap signal.
Revenue +379% at 10.7x P/E is the textbook peak-cycle print. Beta 3.3, 17% below its 50d, CXMT scaling, and no contract-price data. Seven seats own it without checking the one number that matters.
3.9% held into a binary Nov 17 print with a broken trend (8% below 50d). Data-center curbs under the new Congress are an unmodeled policy risk. Together with MSFT, MU and AVGO it is one factor.
3.9% at +43% over 6 months, with drug-pricing exposure under a Democratic Congress. Consensus treats beta -0.11 as uncorrelated, but policy risk is not captured in beta.

cut.reason: Peak-cycle margins, beta 3.3, no contract-price evidence; the risk is unpriced at this size.
Yield-trap risk from the SpaceX entry; TMUS and T show the whole group is under pressure.
0.3% is too small to matter, and it adds debt and MediaTek-rumor risk; cost exceeds benefit.

blind_spots: No seat has modeled the correlation between the defensive stack (VZ, ABBV, V, CB, PFE, XLV, RSP) in a bond rally.
Nobody has data-center policy details under the new Congress; it is unconfirmed and hits MSFT, NVDA and MU together.
The December hike odds of 77% are unconfirmed, so SHY's thesis rests on a number nobody verified.
Eight seats converged on the same five names, which suggests shared reasoning rather than independent evidence.
redteam.killer_scenario: CPI on Nov 10 prints soft and the Fed hike odds collapse, so yields drop and breadth rotates back to mega-cap tech. The defensive stack that is now at highs mean-reverts, while 27% SHY and thin AI exposure lag. Then NVDA guides weak on Nov 17 and MSFT, MU and NVDA fall together.

risk.statement: Largest risk: one factor, AI capex funding plus the rate path, behind MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, META, MU and ANET. Limit: AI-linked names combined at most 16%, because MSFT and NVDA fall together on a hot CPI Nov 10 or weak guide Nov 17. NVDA is capped at 5% for that binary print. MU is capped at 1.5%: revenue +379% is peak-cycle shaped and no contract-price data is in the book. SHY need not exceed 20%; the seats have already cut it. Defensives at RSI 70+ are crowded, so no sector above 30%. Health care is capped at 18% for drug-pricing risk. Cash minimum is 5%, as SHY is cash-like. No vetoes: nothing here shows accounting fraud or illiquidity.
concerns: AI factor: MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, META, ANET, MU move together on a weak NVDA guide Nov 17; keep combined AI under 16%.
CPI Nov 10 against a hiking Fed: a hot print hits long-duration equities, a soft print punishes idle SHY. Size neither side as a certainty.
Defensive crowding: ABBV, V, CB, PFE, RSP, XLV are at highs with RSI 70+ and mean-revert together in a rotation.
Drug-pricing policy under a Democratic Congress is not captured by beta across ABBV, LLY, PFE, XLV, NVO.
Credit: HY spreads up 67bp in three months; financials like JPM and BX are exposed if it continues.

chairRaw.statement: The council will hold 80% in equities, 15% in SHY and 5% in cash, built so that neither a hot nor a soft CPI decides our fate. Three arguments carried this. First, the red team was right: a 27% SHY block was a one-sided rate bet. I cut it to 15%, which is still enough dry powder for the Nov 17 NVDA print. Second, the AI sleeve stays at 14%: MSFT, NVDA and GOOG, under the 16% cap. MSFT holds because it funds itself with $19B of FCF. Third, breadth and cleared catalysts carry the rest: RSP, UBER, JPM and V. I overrule the MU, VZ, ANET and META proposals. Without contract-price data we have no edge, the SpaceX threat is structural, and the caps bind.
chairRaw.summary: This is a balanced first portfolio for a hiking-Fed regime with two dated hinges, CPI on Nov 10 and NVDA on Nov 17. The AI exposure is capped at 14% and anchored by self-funding MSFT. Breadth comes from RSP and from names whose earnings have cleared (UBER, JPM, PFE). A trimmed SHY sleeve serves as dry powder for redeployment after the NVDA print.

atlas.statement: The macro weather is a hiking Fed against 3.7% inflation, and it permits measured risk, but Vex is right that I dressed one bet as a hedge. Because SHY pays about 0.4% over three weeks, a soft CPI on Nov 10 leaves that money idle. I concede and cut SHY to 10%, cut VZ and AVGO, and trim MU. A CPI of 0.2% or lower, or a strong NVDA guide, would move me to add AI risk. My bias is seeing the cycle early.
atlas.regime: Late-cycle stagflation-lite under a hiking Fed; CPI Nov 10 is the hinge, but the SHY hedge was oversized

events.text:
**SCOUT DISPATCH, Wed 4 Nov 2026, about 17:20 GMT**

**1. Lead story: the "blue tsunami" and a violent reversal**
- Democrats won Congress by more than Wall Street expected. 
The size of the blue wave surprised Wall Street, which was expecting a ripple.

- Overnight, 
Nasdaq 100 futures plunged as much as 2.5%
 as the first results came in. They then reversed hard.
- Midday levels: 
Dow 53,306 (+2.9%), S&P 500 7,710 (+1.9%)
. Bloomberg called it the S&P's 
biggest advance in three months.

- Bloomberg also reported that 
Treasury yields fell across the curve, the dollar slipped against all developed-world currencies, Bitcoin topped $80,000 and oil slumped.

- Trump accepted the results. CNBC said that 
removed political uncertainty risk
.
- **Oil:** 
Brent futures traded more than 8% lower
. CNBC reported crude 
below $90 a barrel as Vance blames GOP election defeat on Iran war.
 An Iran war is clearly a live driver of energy prices. I could not confirm the details of the war or the oil path from here.
- **Winners and losers:** Renewables and health stocks rallied. Defense and "neocloud" names lagged. Walmart and Bank of America rose as money rotated away from tech.
- **Regulatory risk for the tech names:** Google Finance reported that 
Tesla and SpaceX fell about 6% early, and Palantir and Intel also dropped, on worries about tougher AI regulation.
 The NBC piece is headed "Democrats vs. data centers". Watch PLTR, TSLA, SPCX, INTC and the AI infrastructure names (NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, ANET). A Democratic Congress can hold hearings, and it can pass bills if it gets support. I could not confirm any specific bill.

**2. Chips: a bear market, then a bounce**
- 
Monday's close left chip stocks in a fresh bear market, below their summer lows and a key technical level.
 SMH and SOXX-type holdings were the pressure point.
- Tuesday brought a bounce: 
the S&P rose 0.4%, the Nasdaq about 0.8%, and the Dow fell about 0.4%.

- **AMD** reported after the close Tuesday and beat the Street. Price reaction is unconfirmed. **Super Micro** 
jumped more than 9%
 after beating on EPS and revenue.
- **SHOP** is the negative surprise. 
It plunged 15% premarket on Tuesday after Q3 revenue and total order value missed.

- CNBC also flagged a Citi "sell" call on a struggling software stock. The name isn't given, so I can't tie it to NOW or CRM.
- **Bold read:** a chip bear market followed by a relief rally on one political event is not yet a trend change. Tonight's ARM and QCOM prints and Nvidia on 17 Nov are the real tests.

**3. The Fed: the market is pricing a hike, not a cut**
- The cut-versus-hike picture is murky and the sources conflict. The most credible read is a **hawkish** one. After the 2 Oct jobs report, CNBC said 
traders still expected a December hike, with FedWatch odds above 75%.

- A separate 2 Nov-dated page said 
a 25 bp hike was 71–73% likely across Polymarket, Kalshi and CME FedWatch
. It also put the odds of zero cuts in 2026 at about 97%.
- One piece from 3 days ago claims over 90% odds of a December cut during a data blackout. That contradicts the rest and looks unreliable, and some of the other pages that came up were stale 2025 articles. **Treat Fed pricing as unconfirmed and check CME FedWatch directly.**
- The FOMC meets 8–9 Dec, or 9–10 Dec per one source. Confirm the date.
- Falling yields and oil today help the case against a hike. A weak payrolls number on Friday would push the same way. A hot CPI would revive the hike case.

**4. Calendar: what matters**
- **Today (4 Nov):** ISM services (consensus 54.8). After the close: ARM, QCOM and MCK. Earlier today: MCD, UBER, CVS, NVO and TM. NVO was already in the premarket movers list, but I could not confirm the direction. MCD results were also flagged by CNBC.
- **Thu 5 Nov:** Energy before the open: COP and CNQ, to see how a sub-$90 Brent flows through to margins. Also PH and SONY.
- **Fri 6 Nov:** Jobs report (consensus 63K). BRK.B reports. Berkshire's cash pile is a sentiment gauge.
- **Tue 10 Nov:** CPI, the key hawk-or-dove print. PBR reports after the close.
- **Wed 11 Nov:** CSCO. **Thu 12 Nov:** AMAT after the close, which is the equipment read-through for LRCX and KLAC.
- **Fri 13 Nov:** PPI. The Japanese banks report: MUFG, SMFG and MFG.
- **Tue 17 Nov:** Retail sales. NVDA after the close is the big event for the AI trade. HD, DIS, BHP, MDT and PDD also report.
- **Wed 18 Nov:** LOW, TJX and PANW. **Thu 19 Nov:** WMT.
- **Tue 24 Nov:** BABA, ADI and DELL. **Wed 25 Nov:** GDP, PCE and DE.
- The 2026 jobs, CPI and PCE data may carry shutdown-related distortions. I could not confirm this.

**5. Sentiment and positioning**
- **Rotation:** Money is moving away from the Magnificent Seven and into cyclicals, small caps and health care. 
The Russell 2000 soared 2%
 at the open. Another headline said the Magnificent Seven "buck the trend", so mega-cap behavior is mixed. Bloomberg's megacap gauge was up 3%.
- **Valuation:** The Nasdaq 100 is up about 40% since Election Day 2024. That is a lot of gains for regulation headlines to threaten.
- **Defense:** CNBC suggested the defense selloff may be a buying opportunity. That is one opinion, not a signal. LMT, RTX and BA could stay soft if Iran war risk fades.
- **Not confirmed:** ETF flows, options positioning and VIX levels. I found no reliable data on any of them.

**Bottom line:** Today's rally is a relief move driven by political clarity and cheaper oil. It does not yet change the underlying risks of a possible Fed hike, a chip bear market and AI regulation. The next real tests are Friday's jobs report, CPI on 10 Nov and NVDA on 17 Nov.

**WISE COUNCIL: SCOUT DISPATCH, Wed 4 Nov 2026, about 17:20 GMT**

**LEAD: A blue wave removes election risk, but AI is the weak spot**

Stocks jumped Wednesday after Democrats won decisively in the midterms and Trump accepted the result. 
The S&P 500 gained 1.7% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.9%.
 
Intraday quotes put the S&P at 7,699.82 and the Dow at 53,282.50, up about 2.9%.
 The overnight swing was large. 
Nasdaq 100 futures were down as much as 2.5% as the first results came in Tuesday night.


The rally is not uniform, and the split matters for the council.
- **AI and data-center names lagged.** 
Nvidia fell 1.5% in early trade and was the heaviest weight on the S&P.
 
CoreWeave dropped about 10% as the Democratic wins hit data-center sentiment.
 The stated risk is that 
any broad slowing of data-center construction could endanger the investments many top companies have made.

- **Other losers:** 
Trump Media fell 12%
 and 
Tesla fell about 3%.

- **Winners:** 
Renewables and health stocks rallied.

- **Volatility and gold:** 
The VIX fell to about 17, and gold rose to about $4,073.

- **Seasonality:** 
Stocks historically do well in the six months after a midterm.
 Yahoo's warning is that the hard part comes next. I could not confirm sector rotation beyond the first hours.

**SENTIMENT: Tech was in a rout before the vote**


At Tuesday's open, 51% of Nasdaq-100 stocks were in a bear market, down 20% or more from highs.
 
Friday's equity sell-off, led by tech, sent investors into Treasurys.
 Chips bounced Tuesday. 
Sandisk, Micron, Intel, Applied Materials, AMD and Arm each rose 3% or more.
 The tape is fragile and two-way.

**THE AI CAPEX VERDICT (last week's prints)**
- **Alphabet:** One outlet reports 
shares sank 11% as capex of $51B pushed free cash flow to negative $9B for a second straight quarter.
 Treat the size of the drop as single-sourced. Another source says Alphabet held its capex guide at 
$195–205B.

- **Microsoft:** 
It trimmed its capex forecast to $170B from $175B.
 
It beat on earnings and revenue, with Azure up 48%.
 
Its CFO said third-party AI chip delays push some capacity into the first half of 2027.
 
Free cash flow was +$19B.

- **Meta:** 
Full-year capex guidance is $135–145B, with the bottom of the range raised.

- **Amazon:** 
It slipped on its report.
 
The concerns are slowing high-margin ad growth and AI agents disintermediating e-commerce.

- **Market read:** 
Investors now focus on cash-flow returns, not on rewarding spend.
 Microsoft is seen as the cleanest funder. Alphabet and Meta are the cash-burn worries.
- **Apple:** It dropped on Election Day. 
It reported on an unusual Monday schedule.
 I could not confirm the cause of the drop.

**MACRO: The Fed is hiking, and that is the key regime fact**
- **The Fed:** 
It held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28, with a 10–2 vote.
 
The two dissenters wanted a quarter-point hike.
 
Chair Kevin Warsh led a unanimous September hike, the first since 2023.

- **December odds (unconfirmed):** One aggregator shows 
a 77.4% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting as of Nov 4.
 I could not cross-check this against CME directly. Another piece cites under 10% for the October meeting, which is a different meeting.
- **Inflation:** 
CPI ran 3.7% year on year in September, up from 3.4%.

- **Yields:** 
The 10-year is about 4.90%, the 2-year 4.57% and the 30-year 5.29%.
 
Last month the 30-year hit 5.47% and the 10-year 5.18%, the highest in decades.
 Treasury sets its auction sizes today.
- **Oil and Iran:** 
The conflict is eight months old, and reports say Washington and Tehran are seeking a diplomatic exit.
 
Brent fell 7.6% Monday to $104.77.
 
Crude fell more than 8% Wednesday after Vance blamed the war for the election losses.
 Brent was at $117 only days ago. A real deal would cut inflation pressure and hurt XOM, CVX, COP and CNQ.
- **Bitcoin:** 
It is about $80,000.


**CALENDAR: Next two weeks, with the confirmed and unconfirmed items**
- **Today, Nov 4:** ISM services (expected 54.8). Earnings: ARM and QCOM after the close, plus CVS, MCD, NVO, UBER, MCK and TM. Treasury auction sizes. Riksbank decision.
- **Thu, Nov 5:** Bank of England and Norges Bank decisions. Earnings: CNQ, COP, PH, SONY.
- **Fri, Nov 6:** Jobs report (consensus 63K). BRK.B earnings. A weak print against a hawkish Fed is the stagflation test.
- **Tue, Nov 10:** 
October CPI at 8:30am New York time.
 
It is the last inflation reading before the Dec 9 meeting.
 This is the decisive macro event of the window.
- **Wed, Nov 11:** CSCO earnings.
- **Thu, Nov 12:** AMAT after the close.
- **Fri, Nov 13:** PPI. MUFG, MFG and SMFG earnings.
- **Tue, Nov 17:** Retail sales. 
NVDA reports after the close, a date marked confirmed by one source.
 
Consensus is EPS $2.47 on revenue of $108.82B.
 
The last quarter was $96.2B, up 106%,
 and 
the stock moved 7% on that print.
 Also HD, DIS, BHP, MDT and PDD.
- **Wed, Nov 18:** 
FOMC minutes at 2:00pm ET.
 LOW, TJX and PANW (after the close).
- **Thu, Nov 19:** WMT.
- **Nov 24–25:** BABA, ADI and DELL on the 24th. GDP, PCE and DE on the 25th.
- **Dec 9:** FOMC, just beyond the window.

**EARNINGS CONTEXT**
- Zacks reports tech Q3 earnings up 
+42.5% on +30.1% revenue, with 84.1% beating EPS estimates.
 
Excluding Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet, S&P growth falls to +26.5% from +43.4%.
 Fundamentals are strong, but the market is punishing the cash burn.
- AMD: 
It reported much stronger profit than expected but rose only modestly.
 
It is paying OpenAI and Meta in stock.

- Super Micro: 
It jumped more than 9% after beating estimates.

- SpaceX (SPCX): 
It signed a deal with Qualcomm and is nearing status as a fourth US carrier. Shares fell about 3%.


**BOLD READ**
The election gave a relief bid, but the real drivers are three things. The first is the CPI print on Nov 10 against a Fed that wants to hike. The second is oil and any Iran deal. The third is whether Nvidia on Nov 17 can restore faith in AI spending. Cheap, battered chips and memory are bouncing, while hyperscaler free cash flow and data-center policy remain open questions. Renewables, health care and rate-sensitive domestic names are the policy-clarity beneficiaries.

**Unconfirmed:**
- The Alphabet drop size.
- The December hike odds.
- Midterm policy details such as data-center rules.
- The specific causes of Apple's and Amazon's moves.

Because CPI is 3.7%, the 10-year sits at 4.9% with a real yield of 2.6%, and a hike near 77% priced for December (unconfirmed), rates are the binding constraint on valuation. The election relief rally is real but breadth, not the Nasdaq, is carrying it. I hold substantial cash and short-dated Treasuries, plus low-beta health care and staples, banks, and a modest energy hedge against an Iran deal failing. My bias is seeing the cycle early; a CPI print on Nov 10 at or below 0.2% month on month, with yields falling, would make me add risk. A hot print or a 10-year above 5.2% would cut it.

data.statement: Four sessions to CPI on Nov 10, eleven to NVDA on Nov 17. Vex is right on three points and I move. MU is cut to zero: the peak-cycle risk has no contract-price evidence and the print that tells us is not mine to guess. VZ is cut to 3%: SpaceX-Qualcomm is a thesis-changing event, and TMUS and T falling on it is the signal. AVGO was never held. SHY drops to 14%, because a soft CPI plus a strong NVDA guide punishes idle cash. I keep MSFT at 6% and NVDA at 3% as the dated AI sleeve. The proceeds go to RSP and UBER, whose events are already cleared. My bias is to chase headlines, so I cap every position at 6%.

data.statement: Largest risk: one factor, AI capex funding plus the rate path, behind MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, META, MU and ANET. Limit: AI-linked names combined at most 16%, because MSFT and NVDA fall together on a hot CPI Nov 10 or weak guide Nov 17. NVDA is capped at 5% for that binary print. MU is capped at 1.5%: revenue +379% is peak-cycle shaped and no contract-price data is in the book. SHY need not exceed 20%; the seats have already cut it. Defensives at RSI 70+ are crowded, so no sector above 30%. Health care is capped at 18% for drug-pricing risk. Cash minimum is 5%, as SHY is cash-like. No vetoes: nothing here shows accounting fraud or illiquidity.
concerns: AI factor: MSFT, NVDA, GOOG, META, ANET, MU move together on a weak NVDA guide Nov 17; keep combined AI under 16%.
CPI Nov 10 against a hiking Fed: a hot print hits long-duration equities, a soft print punishes idle SHY. Size neither side as a certainty.
Defensive crowding: ABBV, V, CB, PFE, RSP, XLV are at highs with RSI 70+ and mean-revert together in a rotation.
Drug-pricing policy under a Democratic Congress is not captured by beta across ABBV, LLY, PFE, XLV, NVO.
Credit: HY spreads up 67bp in three months; financials like JPM and BX are exposed if it continues.

data.statement: The council will hold 80% in equities, 15% in SHY and 5% in cash, built so that neither a hot nor a soft CPI decides our fate. Three arguments carried this. First, the red team was right: a 27% SHY block was a one-sided rate bet. I cut it to 15%, which is still enough dry powder for the Nov 17 NVDA print. Second, the AI sleeve stays at 14%: MSFT, NVDA and GOOG, under the 16% cap. MSFT holds because it funds itself with $19B of FCF. Third, breadth and cleared catalysts carry the rest: RSP, UBER, JPM and V. I overrule the MU, VZ, ANET and META proposals. Without contract-price data we have no edge, the SpaceX threat is structural, and the caps bind.
data.summary: This is a balanced first portfolio for a hiking-Fed regime with two dated hinges, CPI on Nov 10 and NVDA on Nov 17. The AI exposure is capped at 14% and anchored by self-funding MSFT. Breadth comes from RSP and from names whose earnings have cleared (UBER, JPM, PFE). A trimmed SHY sleeve serves as dry powder for redeployment after the NVDA print.

data.changes: This is the first portfolio, built from $100,000. Relative to consensus, I cut SHY to 15% and kept cash at 5%. I dropped MU, VZ, META, ANET, BX, HD and XLV, because of caps, the absence of contract-price data, the SpaceX threat or overbought crowding. I capped the AI sleeve at 14%, below the 16% limit. I added NVO and TJX for dated, rate-independent catalysts, and raised RSP to 10% to own the breadth.

dissent.view: Wanted SHY at 10% plus MU, BX and HD as soft-CPI offsets; I kept more dry powder and rejected MU without contract-price data.
Wanted NVO at 7% and a token MU stake; NVO was cut to 3% for drug-pricing concentration, and MU was excluded.
Wanted ANET at 4%; at 182x P/E it would push the AI factor past the risk manager's 16% limit.
Wanted META, VZ and TMUS; META would breach the AI limit, and the SpaceX carrier threat makes the telecom yield a possible trap.
Wanted SHY at 17%; I judged 15% plus 5% cash sufficient for the two dated binaries.
Wanted TMO and WELL as trend leaders; I declined to add more crowded, rate-sensitive defensives at highs.

watch: CPI on Nov 10: a print of 0.2% or lower leads to redeploying SHY; 0.4% or higher means trimming RSP and MSFT.
NVDA on Nov 17 against $108.8B revenue consensus; this decides whether to add to AI up to the 16% cap.
HY spread: above 4.0pp triggers a review of JPM and RSP.
Brent and the US-Iran talks: a signed deal means exiting TTE.
Drug-pricing moves by the new Congress across ABBV, PFE, LLY and NVO.
